clue.text: Doddery ex-judge with SUV, one safe to take a chance at the wheel!

definitions.text: take a chance at the wheel!
definitions.note: an instruction to bet, not a verb phrase in the same form

indicators.note: a doddery person totters unsteadily, so the letters wobble out of their order

blocks.note: EX as written, plus J, the abbreviation for judge
taken as written
Roman numeral for one
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A shaky old retired judge, sitting in a big safe car, decides to gamble by driving it himself.
explanation.walkthrough: 'At the wheel' suggests driving, but the wheel is a roulette wheel. FAITES VOS JEUX is French for 'place your bets', the croupier's call before the spin.
explanation.definitionFit: The croupier's French call invites players to stake money on the roulette spin, which is gambling on that casino device.

clue.text: Vain female of no fixed abode, reportedly

indicators.note: what is reported is passed on by word of mouth, so the solver goes by the sound

blocks.note: standard abbreviation for female
having no fixed home means being without roots

explanation.surface: A conceited homeless woman is described in some report.
explanation.walkthrough: F plus ROOTLESS, said aloud, gives FRUITLESS. 'Vain' looks like conceited, but here it means futile.
explanation.definitionFit: Vain in the sense of useless or unsuccessful matches efforts that produce no result, bearing nothing.

clue.text: Vessel’s chief engineer stole aboard it

indicators.note: things aboard a ship are carried inside it, so these letters go within the other piece

blocks.note: the initials of chief engineer, a ship's senior engineering officer
a boa is a long scarf or stole of feathers or fur
taken as written

explanation.surface: A ship's chief engineer has stowed away on board.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stole' reads as the past tense of steal, but it is the noun, a scarf.
explanation.definitionFit: An iceboat is a vessel, either one that sails on runners over ice or one that breaks a channel through it.

clue.text: To be sure, an unusual resort!

indicators.note: something unusual is out of the ordinary, so these letters leave their ordinary order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone exclaims that a holiday town is certainly an odd one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'To be sure' reads as a stock phrase of agreement, but all its letters feed the wordplay. EASTBOURNE is a seaside town in Sussex, on England's south coast.
explanation.definitionFit: Eastbourne is a long-established English seaside holiday town, so it is an example of a resort.

clue.text: Tested by speaking through journalist, maintaining volume

indicators.note: to maintain something is to keep hold of it, so one piece holds another

blocks.note: via means by way of, through
standard abbreviation for volume
ED, short for editor, is the usual crossword journalist

explanation.surface: Someone was quizzed out loud through a reporter, keeping the sound level up.
explanation.walkthrough: To viva is to examine orally, from Latin viva voce, as at the end of a doctorate; the verb's past form looks odd but is standard.
explanation.definitionFit: A viva is an oral examination, so someone vivaed has been examined through spoken questions rather than writing.

clue.text: Girl about to drain a stream to find plant root

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece wraps round the rest

blocks.note: a girl's name
to sap is to drain of strength
taken as written
a rill is a small stream

explanation.surface: A girl sets out to dry up a brook in search of a root.
explanation.walkthrough: 'To drain' looks like the purpose of the girl's trip, but it is just a synonym inside her name, and 'to find' is the link.
explanation.definitionFit: Sarsaparilla is the dried root of a tropical vine, used to flavour drinks and in old remedies.

clue.text: Out of The Times, text (English) gets its interpretation

indicators.note: T stands for time, so every instance of 'times' is taken out of the letters that follow

blocks.note: taken as written
standard abbreviation for English
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: An extract from The Times newspaper is explained to readers.
explanation.walkthrough: TEXT E GETS ITS loses all four Ts to leave EXEGESIS. 'The Times' looks like the newspaper, but it means the letter T, several times over.
explanation.definitionFit: Exegesis is critical explanation of a text, especially scripture, which is a kind of interpretation.

clue.text: Picture accompanied by an echo in Cineplex?

definitions.text: accompanied by an echo in Cineplex?
definitions.note: describes a letter's code word, not a picture

blocks.note: first meaning: a radiograph image

blocks.clueFragment: accompanied by an echo in Cineplex?
blocks.note: second meaning: the radio-alphabet word for the last letter of the cinema word, which has Echo, its E, right beside it

explanation.surface: A film plays in a cinema with a sound echo.
explanation.walkthrough: In the NATO phonetic alphabet E is Echo and X is X-ray; in CINEPLEX the X stands next to the E. An X-ray is also a picture.
explanation.definitionFit: An X-ray is a medical image made with radiation, so it is a kind of photograph or picture.

clue.text: Yankee in game show to disregard the score?

indicators.note: placed in means put inside, so one letter sits within a longer piece

blocks.note: a play is a game
Yankee is Y in the radio alphabet
to bear a mark is to show it

explanation.surface: An American on a TV quiz ignores the points tally.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Score' suggests a game total, but it is written music. 'Game show' looks like one TV phrase but splits into two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: To play by ear is to perform music without reading the written notes, so the printed music is ignored.

clue.text: Occupier not normally dealt with so blooming early!

indicators.note: handled abnormally, these letters are not kept in their usual order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A tenant handled in an unusual way flowers ahead of time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dealt with' reads as a matter handled, but it marks a reshuffle of the two words before it.
explanation.definitionFit: Precocious first described plants flowering or fruiting before the usual season, then children developing ahead of their age.

clue.text: Clip with article on Irish town

blocks.note: an indefinite article
to clip is to trim

explanation.surface: A cutting with a newspaper piece about a town in Ireland.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'on' puts the article above the other piece. ANTRIM is a town, and county, in Northern Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: Antrim is a town in Northern Ireland, county town of the county of the same name, so it fits the place description.

clue.text: Pair of shades a boxer gets after fight?

definitions.note: describes the state the boxer ends up in, an adjective

blocks.note: first meaning: two colours named together
second meaning: covered in bruises

explanation.walkthrough: 'Pair of shades' tempts one to think of sunglasses; it is two colours.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase lists two dark colours, and as an idiom it describes someone heavily bruised after a beating.

clue.text: Coup on course, finally, since junta taking full charge

indicators.note: finally points to the end of each of the following words, so only their closing letters count

blocks.note: the closing letter of each of these five words

explanation.surface: A military takeover is finally done since a ruling junta has seized total control.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coup' reads as a political takeover, which the rest of the surface supports; on a golf course it is a triumph.
explanation.definitionFit: In golf an eagle is two strokes under par on a hole, a notable stroke of success on the course.

clue.text: Picture of mine follows

blocks.note: a mine of information is a rich store or reservoir
to dog someone is to follow them

explanation.surface: A painting of a pit comes next.
explanation.walkthrough: Picture means a film here: Reservoir Dogs is Quentin Tarantino's 1992 crime movie.
explanation.definitionFit: Picture is a common word for a cinema film, and this title is a well-known Tarantino feature film.

clue.text: Clients American and Irish mostly

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the final letter is dropped

blocks.note: standard abbreviation for American
Erse is the Irish (Gaelic) language

explanation.surface: The customers are largely from the USA and Ireland.
explanation.walkthrough: Irish here is the language, Erse, which loses its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Clients of a service or product are the people who use it, so the two words are close synonyms.

clue.text: After adjusting VAT, I agree to diversify

indicators.note: adjusting means altering, so the letters are altered into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone agrees, once the tax rate is changed, to branch out into new areas.
explanation.walkthrough: VAT is Britain's value added tax, a sales tax; here it is just three letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To variegate is to give variety to, especially by marking with different colours, so it means making more varied.

clue.text: What gets viewers streaming talk on race?

blocks.note: to tear along is to race
gas is idle talk

explanation.surface: A TV pundit wonders what gets audiences streaming a programme about a horse race.
explanation.walkthrough: Viewers are eyes and streaming means watering, not watching online. In an across clue 'talk on race' puts talk after race.
explanation.definitionFit: Tear gas irritates the eyes and makes them water heavily, which is how it disperses crowds.

clue.text: Agitator close to corrupt and profitable St Petersburg concern?

indicators.note: the close of a word is its end, so only its final letter is wanted

blocks.note: the final letter of this word
a Russian business that makes money would make roubles, Russia's currency

explanation.surface: A rabble-rouser is near a crooked, lucrative business in Russia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Corrupt and profitable' looks like a description of the business, but 'close to corrupt' supplies one letter and the question mark flags the invented money-maker.
explanation.definitionFit: An agitator stirs up unrest and discontent, which is exactly what a troublemaker does.

clue.text: Alaskan native, one captured by camera naked, we understand

indicators.note: something captured is held inside its captor, so one piece goes into another
what we understand is what we have heard said, so the sound counts, not the spelling

blocks.note: Kodak is a famous camera brand
Roman numeral for one
bare means naked

explanation.surface: An Inuit person is snapped by a photographer without any clothes on, apparently.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Alaskan native' suggests a person, but it is an animal native to Alaska.
explanation.definitionFit: The Kodiak bear is a huge brown bear found only on the Kodiak islands of Alaska, so it is native there.

clue.text: Don’t have your fare home?

blocks.note: surface: a passenger who lacks money for the journey back
setter's reading: fare is food, so this is about not taking your meal in your own house

explanation.walkthrough: Fare suggests a ticket price, so the clue seems to be about being stranded; fare also means food.
explanation.definitionFit: To dine at a restaurant rather than in one's own house is to take one's food somewhere other than home.

clue.text: A short journey by about six with a pilot

indicators.note: something cut short has lost its tail, so the final letter goes
about means around, so the earlier pieces surround the next ones

blocks.note: taken as written
a trip is a journey
by as in multiplication, the times sign X
Roman numeral for six
taken as written

explanation.surface: A quick outing at around six o'clock with someone who flies planes.
explanation.walkthrough: By means times, as in three by four, so it gives the multiplication sign. 'With' joins six to the following letter before both go inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Aviatrix is an old-fashioned word for a woman who flies aircraft, a female pilot.

clue.text: Period assigned by group

blocks.note: by as in multiplication: three by four is three times four
a lot is a group or batch

explanation.surface: A spell of time allotted by a committee.
explanation.walkthrough: 'By' reads as 'by whom', but it is the multiplication word, as in a room ten by twelve. The word break moves one letter across.
explanation.definitionFit: A time slot is an allocated interval in a schedule, such as a broadcasting period or appointment.

clue.text: All closed following digging?

indicators.note: following means coming after, so the piece named first in the clue is placed second

blocks.note: slang: if you dig something you are into it
a door pulled to is closed

explanation.surface: Everything shut down after an excavation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Following' puts the closed piece after the digging one. Digging is sixties slang for liking.
explanation.definitionFit: In toto is Latin for 'in total', meaning altogether or completely, as in all of it.

clue.text: What experts know about“unknowns” — answer: they’re negative!

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece is wrapped round the others

blocks.note: an expert is said to know their onions
x and y are the usual unknowns in algebra
standard abbreviation for answer

explanation.surface: Specialists insist that unknown quantities always turn out to be bad news.
explanation.walkthrough: To know your onions is a British idiom for being knowledgeable. The definition is a cryptic description: these are negatively charged.
explanation.definitionFit: Oxyanions are negatively charged ions containing oxygen, such as sulfate, so they carry a negative charge.

clue.text: Imaginary line bats also go in

indicators.note: bats is slang for crazy, and crazy letters are out of their proper order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Bats fly in along an invisible line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bats' looks like the flying animals, the subject of the sentence, but it is an adjective meaning mad.
explanation.definitionFit: An isogonal is a line on a map joining points of equal magnetic declination, a line drawn but not physically present.

clue.text: Fielder is behind boundary

blocks.note: to second a motion is to back it, so one who is behind it seconds it
a lip is an edge or rim

explanation.surface: A cricketer stands back from the edge of the field.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boundary' sounds like cricket's edge of the field, but it is just a rim. In cricket, second slip is a fielder standing beside the wicketkeeper.
explanation.definitionFit: Second slip is a cricket fielding position, so the player stationed there is a fielder.

clue.text: Cheated-on duke seen in mostly foolish light

indicators.note: what is seen in something appears inside it, so one letter sits within another piece
mostly means not quite all, so the last letter is lost

blocks.note: cuckoo means crazy or foolish
an LED is a light-emitting diode, a small light
standard abbreviation for duke

explanation.surface: A duke whose wife strayed looks rather ridiculous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Light' looks like an adjective after 'foolish', but it is a noun, a lamp. The cuckoo, which lays eggs in other birds' nests, gives the word its origin.
explanation.definitionFit: A cuckolded husband is one whose wife has been unfaithful, so he has been cheated on.

clue.text: One taking on fancy goods?

blocks.note: surface: someone who stocks luxury or ornamental merchandise
setter's reading: fancy is a whim, so this person acquires things on a sudden whim

explanation.walkthrough: 'Fancy goods' reads as decorative stock; split the phrase so fancy means a passing whim.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who purchases things on a sudden whim, without planning, is acquiring goods because of a fancy.

clue.text: Give time to son to finish drink

blocks.note: standard abbreviation for son
end means finish
to down a drink is to swallow it

explanation.surface: A parent allows their son some time to finish his drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Give time' sounds generous, but time here is a prison term. Send down is British for sentencing to jail, and also for expelling from university.
explanation.definitionFit: A judge who sends a convict down gives them a prison sentence, which is serving time.

clue.text: Love to meet with tart in uniform

indicators.note: placed in means put inside, so one piece sits within another

blocks.note: love is nil in tennis, the letter O
to face someone is to meet them
a tart is a kind of pie

explanation.surface: A sweetheart arranges to meet someone, pastry in hand, while wearing a uniform.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Uniform' looks like clothing, the noun; it is the adjective meaning consistent.
explanation.definitionFit: Things of a piece are consistent with each other and alike throughout, so they are uniform in character.

clue.text: White pawn

blocks.note: first meaning: a German white wine from the Rhine
second meaning: to leave something with a pawnbroker for a loan

explanation.walkthrough: 'White pawn' reads as a chess piece; it is two separate words. Hock is the British name for Rhine wine.
explanation.definitionFit: Hock is a white Rhenish wine, and to hock something is slang for pawning it for cash.

clue.text: Find oneself shy following school dance

indicators.note: following means coming after, so the piece named next in the clue is placed in front

blocks.note: a high school
to land up somewhere is to find oneself there
to shy a stone is to throw or fling it

explanation.surface: A timid pupil feels awkward after the school disco.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shy' reads as timid, but it is the verb to throw. 'Following school' puts the school piece first.
explanation.definitionFit: The Highland fling is a lively solo Scottish country dance, so it is a type of dance.

clue.text: Fancy swimmer’s former, cracking girlfriend, rather!

indicators.note: to crack something is to break into it, so one piece goes inside another

blocks.note: standard abbreviation for girlfriend
old means former, as in an old flame
-ish means rather or somewhat, and is used alone in casual speech

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether you rather fancy a swimmer's ex, who is breaking up with his new partner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fancy' reads as a verb of desire; in fact fancy goldfish are ornamental breeds with odd fins and bodies.
explanation.definitionFit: A fancy goldfish is one of the ornamental breeds of this fish, so it is a decorative swimming creature.

clue.text: Suggestion from local United goal offside, initially

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so only the opening letter of the word is taken

blocks.note: your local is your nearest pub, an inn
standard abbreviation for United, as in football club names
an end is an aim or goal
the first letter of this word

explanation.surface: A pub-goer hints that a home team's goal was offside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Goal' looks like football, but it means an aim. In Britain your local is the pub nearest home.
explanation.definitionFit: Innuendo is an indirect hint, usually suggestive or disparaging, so it is a veiled suggestion.

clue.text: Serializes broadcast about football managers without interference

indicators.note: to broadcast seed is to scatter it, so these letters are scattered into a new order
about means around, so the shuffled letters go round the other piece

blocks.note: taken as written
the FA, the Football Association, governs English football

explanation.surface: A TV channel puts out a serial about football bosses who are left alone to do as they like.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Football managers' suggests club bosses, but it is the governing body. 'Broadcast' reads as TV, not as a scattering.
explanation.definitionFit: Laissez-faire, French for 'let do', is a policy of leaving things alone and not intervening.

clue.text: Bursting with energy, following fine learning guide

blocks.note: standard abbreviation for energy
standard abbreviation for following, as in 'pp 10 f'
pencil grade abbreviation for fine
lore is learning or traditional knowledge
a scent guides a hound, as a trail does

explanation.surface: An eager pupil follows a good study guide, full of energy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bursting with energy' looks like the whole definition, but only the first word defines; 'following' is a letter, not an order word.
explanation.definitionFit: Efflorescent means bursting into flower, or forming a powdery crust, so it describes something breaking out.

clue.text: In vain, go off to find John in Rome?

indicators.note: food gone off is spoilt, so these letters are spoilt out of their order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone sets off without success to look for a man called John in the Italian capital.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks a definition by example: the name is Italian.
explanation.definitionFit: Giovanni is the Italian form of the name John, so it is what a John would be called in Italy.

clue.text: Readily supplied with pet by FBI agent

blocks.note: to spoon is old slang for petting, kissing and cuddling
a fed is US slang for a federal agent

explanation.surface: Someone was conveniently provided with an animal by a federal officer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pet' reads as a household animal, but it is the verb to cuddle.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone spoon-fed is handed everything without effort, as a baby is fed, so it means readily supplied.

clue.text: Reptiles biting tail off crow

indicators.note: with its tail off, a word loses its final letter

blocks.note: to crow is to boast

explanation.surface: Snakes are snapping the tail off a black bird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crow' looks like a bird, the reptiles' prey, but it is the verb to brag.
explanation.definitionFit: Boas are large constricting snakes, and snakes are reptiles, so these are examples of the class.

clue.text: Cheerful party assessed finally to have flipped

indicators.note: finally points to the end of the word, so only its closing letter is used

blocks.note: up means in good spirits
a side is a party in a dispute
the final letter of this word
to own is to have

explanation.surface: A jolly celebration, judged at last, seems to have gone wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Party' reads as a celebration, which suits 'cheerful'; it is a side in a contest.
explanation.definitionFit: Something flipped over has been turned so its top is underneath, which is what being inverted means.

clue.text: Revealing bishop’s responsibility at an end

blocks.note: a see is the diocese a bishop is responsible for
through means finished

explanation.surface: A churchman exposes that a bishop's duties are finished.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revealing' looks like a verb about disclosure; it is the adjective for thin clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: Revealing clothes show the body, and see-through fabric is transparent enough to show what is underneath.

clue.text: Bloomer: one by boy per year is disturbing

indicators.note: something disturbing intrudes and breaks in, so this letter forces its way into the other pieces

blocks.note: 'one' is another bloomer, a slip or mistake, here one made by a lad, so a lad's slip
taken as written
standard abbreviation for year

explanation.surface: A boy's yearly blunder is upsetting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bloomer' first reads as a mistake, and 'one' picks that sense up; but as the definition it is something that blooms, a flower.
explanation.definitionFit: The lady's-slipper is an orchid with a pouch-shaped lip, so it is a flowering plant, something that blooms.

clue.text: Career criminal enters without being spotted

indicators.note: whatever enters goes inside, so one piece is placed within the other

blocks.note: to career is to rush along, to fly
a criminal act is lawless

explanation.surface: A habitual crook breaks in and nobody sees him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Career criminal' reads as one phrase; split it, and career is the verb to hurtle. 'Spotted' means marked with spots, not seen.
explanation.definitionFit: Flawlessly means perfectly, with no blemish or mark, so the work done carries no spot.

clue.text: Metal club Yorkshireman holds back symbolically

definitions.note: describes the element's chemical symbol, not the metal itself

blocks.note: first meaning: a rare-earth metallic element
second meaning: the element whose symbol is Yb, and the run 'cluB Yorkshireman' read backwards holds those two letters

explanation.surface: A Yorkshire golfer keeps his iron in reserve.
explanation.walkthrough: Only the symbol is spelt out: the last letter of club and first of Yorkshireman, reversed, make Yb, and 'symbolically' says the solver must name the element it stands for.
explanation.definitionFit: Ytterbium is a soft silvery rare-earth element, one of the lanthanides, so it is a metal.

clue.text: Welcome not often seen for rising church priest

indicators.note: in a down clue rising means going upwards, so the letters read from bottom to top

blocks.note: hi is a greeting
something rare is seldom seen
standard abbreviation for church

explanation.surface: A rare greeting is offered to a priest who is going up in the church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rising church priest' suggests a cleric getting promoted; rising only acts on the letters before it.
explanation.definitionFit: A hierarch is a chief priest or high-ranking member of the clergy, so the word names a senior priest.

clue.text: Reminders, such as demand for payment, returned by Society

indicators.note: something returned goes back the way it came, so the letters run backwards

blocks.note: e.g., for example, means such as
a dun is a demand for a debt to be paid
standard abbreviation for society

explanation.surface: Reminder letters, including demands for payment, are sent back by a club.
explanation.walkthrough: A dun is an old word for an insistent request for money owed.
explanation.definitionFit: A nudge is a gentle prod or hint that reminds someone to act, so nudges are reminders.

clue.text: Expected more care for one stretched on couch?

blocks.note: to care for something is to like it
someone lying down is a lier

explanation.surface: A patient on a therapist's couch expected more attention.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Expected more' reads as a past-tense verb; it is a comparative adjective. The question mark covers the invented word for a person lying down.
explanation.definitionFit: Likelier is the comparative of likely, describing something that is more probable, more to be anticipated.

clue.text: Maximum to be got from cashpoint — large amount, ultimately

indicators.note: ultimately means in the end, so only the final letter is kept

blocks.note: an ATM, an automated teller machine, is a cashpoint
OS, outsize, is the clothing label for large
the final letter of this word

explanation.surface: The most you can take from a cash machine is a big sum, in the end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Large amount' looks like one phrase, but large is an outsize label and amount supplies a letter. A cashpoint is the British word for a cash machine.
explanation.definitionFit: At most means at the maximum, setting an upper limit, so it matches the definition used adverbially.

clue.text: Island abroad where Scot’s entire family at home?

definitions.text: where Scot’s entire family at home?
definitions.note: a whimsical phrase, not a place description

blocks.note: first meaning: an island in a foreign country

blocks.clueFragment: where Scot’s entire family at home?
blocks.note: second meaning: read as Scots speech, the name splits into an exclamation, 'kin' for family and 'awa' for all, as if a Scot were remarking on the whole family

explanation.walkthrough: The second half is a playful reading of the name as Scottish dialect, kin being family; the question mark admits how loose the fit is.

clue.text: Grass verges on Severn are dying

indicators.note: verges are edges, so only the outermost letters of the word are kept

blocks.note: the first and last letters of this word
to be dying to do something is to itch to do it

explanation.walkthrough: 'Grass verges' reads as roadside lawns; grass is British slang for an informer. The Severn is Britain's longest river.
explanation.definitionFit: To grass on someone is British slang for informing to police, and a snitch is likewise an informer.

clue.text: Fairy’s loose garment moving right down leg

indicators.note: in a down clue moving something down sends it to the bottom, so the right letter goes from top to end

blocks.note: a robe is a loose garment
in cricket the leg side is also called the on side

explanation.surface: A fairy's flowing gown slips down her leg.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Right' looks like the side of the body, but it is R, the letter that moves. Oberon is the fairy king in A Midsummer Night's Dream.
explanation.definitionFit: Oberon is king of the fairies in Shakespeare's A Midsummer Night's Dream, so he is a fairy.

clue.text: Index reference in German on Italian writer

indicators.note: in an across clue one thing on another comes after it, so the order of the parts is turned

blocks.note: Dario Fo, Italian playwright and Nobel laureate
REF is the usual abbreviation for reference
taken as written
standard abbreviation for German

explanation.surface: An index entry points to a German text about an Italian author.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Index reference' reads as a book index; index is the pointing finger. Dario Fo won the 1997 Nobel Prize for Literature.
explanation.definitionFit: The index finger is the first finger next to the thumb, also called the forefinger, used for pointing.

clue.text: Go on before the end to become a minister

indicators.note: stopping before the end means the final letter is never reached

blocks.note: to rabbit on is British slang for talking at tedious length

explanation.surface: Someone is urged to press on to the finish and be ordained.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Go on' reads as an encouragement to continue; it means chatter, as in British 'rabbit on'.
explanation.definitionFit: A rabbi is the religious leader and teacher of a Jewish congregation, so he is a minister of religion.

clue.text: One calling round as hotel bar runs check on reservation

indicators.note: to go round something is to surround it, so one piece encloses the rest

blocks.note: a crier calls out announcements
taken as written
Hotel is H in the radio alphabet
taken as written
standard cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A visitor calls at a hotel bar to confirm a booking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reservation' suggests a booking; it is the central reservation, British for a motorway's median strip.
explanation.definitionFit: A crash barrier stops vehicles crossing the central strip of a motorway, so it is a check placed there.

clue.text: Walk that’s covered three fifths of Spain?

indicators.note: a fraction of a five-letter word marks off a run of its letters, here the opening three

blocks.note: the first letter of the country's name, where the run of letters starts
the run is described as going from one letter to another, and that word is written in
the third letter of the country's name, where the run of letters stops

explanation.surface: A long hike that has crossed much of Spain.
explanation.walkthrough: S, P, A are three of the five letters of SPAIN, and a run of letters from S to A is written out literally as S TO A.
explanation.definitionFit: A stoa is a roofed colonnade in ancient Greek architecture, a sheltered walkway for strolling in.

clue.text: Constituent, one left to enter popular objection

indicators.note: to enter is to go inside, so these letters are placed within the next piece

blocks.note: in means fashionable or popular
but is an objection, as in no ifs or buts
Roman numeral for one
standard abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: A voter, the only one remaining, steps in to make a popular objection.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Constituent' reads as a voter, the noun; it is the adjective meaning forming part of something.
explanation.definitionFit: Something inbuilt is integral, forming an essential part of the whole, which is what constituent means as an adjective.

clue.text: Ruined are our wet waterproofs, etc

indicators.note: something ruined is wrecked, so the letters are wrecked into a new arrangement

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone laments that their soaked rain jackets are spoilt.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition by example, ending 'etc', says the answer is a wider class including waterproofs.
explanation.definitionFit: Outerwear is clothing worn over other garments outdoors, such as coats and rain jackets.

clue.text: On reflection, claim amusement displays taste

indicators.note: a reflection in a mirror shows things backwards, so the letters run the other way
to display is to show openly, so the letters are on view within the words

blocks.note: the letters spanning the two words

explanation.surface: After thinking it over, a person says their enjoyment shows good judgement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Taste' reads as discernment; it is one of the basic flavours.
explanation.definitionFit: Umami is the savoury fifth basic flavour, alongside sweet, sour, salty and bitter, detected by the tongue.

clue.text: Bird with old bit of gold and blueish plumage, brown at the ends

indicators.note: the end of each word is its last letter, so only those are kept

blocks.note: a guinea was an old British gold coin worth 21 shillings
the final letter of each of these three words

explanation.surface: A bird with a flash of gold and blue-grey feathers tipped with brown.
explanation.walkthrough: The colour words look like a description of the bird, which helps the surface, but only their last letters count.
explanation.definitionFit: A guinea hen is a female guineafowl, a speckled grey game bird from Africa.

clue.text: When feverish at home, you briefly prepare tonic

indicators.note: briefly means cut short, so the final letter is dropped

blocks.note: as means when, as in 'as I arrived'
a feverish person is hot
in means at home
thee is an old form of you
to arm is to prepare for conflict

explanation.surface: When you have a fever and are stuck at home, quickly make yourself a restorative drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tonic' suggests a medicinal drink, which suits the feverish scene; it is the figurative sense of a boost.
explanation.definitionFit: A shot in the arm is an idiom for a boost or stimulus, and a tonic likewise means something that invigorates.
